p.src: At that time, Song Jiang, observing from high ground that the Liao army was formidable, hurriedly turned his horse and returned to his own lines, ordering the troops to withdraw and encamp at the mountain pass outside Yongqing County. In his tent he conferred with Lu Junyi, Wu Yong, Gongsun Sheng, and the others, saying, “Though we won today’s engagement and slew two of their vanguard commanders, when I surveyed the Liao forces from the heights, I saw them advancing in overwhelming numbers, covering heaven and earth. This is the main host of the northern army. Tomorrow we must surely meet them in a great battle. I fear our few cannot withstand their many. What are we to do?” Wu Yong replied, “The skilled commanders of old could make a small force withstand a great one. In former times, Xie Xuan of Jin led fifty thousand men and routed Fu Jian’s mighty host of a million. Why should you fear, Vanguard Commander? Issue orders to every commander and soldier that tomorrow the banners must be properly arrayed, bows and crossbows strung, blades drawn, chevaux-de-frise planted deep, and the camp vigilantly guarded. Let the moats and trenches be made ready, every weapon deployed, and scaling ladders, stone-throwers, and the like put in order beforehand. We shall again deploy the Nine Palaces and Eight Trigrams formation. If they attack it, each section will rise in turn; even with a million men, how would they dare break through?” Song Jiang said, “Your counsel is excellent, Strategist.” The orders were immediately issued, and all commanders and troops obeyed them. They cooked their meal at the fifth watch, struck camp at daybreak, and advanced to the borders of Changping County, where they deployed the army and established their camp. The cavalry arrayed in front was still the Tiger force: the great general Qin Ming stood foremost, with Huyan Zhuo behind him; Guan Sheng held the left and Lin Chong the right; Suo Chao took the southeast, Xu Ning the northeast, Dong Ping the southwest, and Yang Zhi the northwest. Song Jiang commanded the central army; the other commanders each retained their former posts; and the infantry formed a separate array in the rear, under Lu Junyi, Lu Zhishen, and Wu Song. Among those tens of thousands were commanders seasoned in countless battles; every man flexed his fists and rubbed his palms, eager for the fight. With the formation settled, they waited solely for the northern army.

p.src: Before long, they saw the Liao army approaching in the distance. At its head came six companies of northern cavalry, five hundred in each, three on the left and three on the right, circling back and forth in a constantly shifting disposition. These six mobile companies were also called the “road scouts” and the “formation guards.” Then the main host came sweeping over the land. The vanguard carried only black standard-banners and formed seven banner gates, each containing a thousand horsemen under a great general. How were they attired? They wore black helmets and dark armor, with black robes over them, and rode black horses. Each bore the same kind of weapon, corresponding exactly to the seven northern lodges: Dipper, Ox, Girl, Emptiness, Rooftop, Encampment, and Wall. Within the seven gates was one supreme commander, corresponding to the celestial Black Tortoise and Water Planet of the North. How was he attired? Fine black hair hung over his head, while a yellow brow-band held a golden circlet tightly in place; he wore a sleeveless black robe, and beneath his glossy black armor lay close-fitted silver mail. He bestrode a black thousand-li courser and brandished a three-pointed blade with a black haft. This was the northern general Quli Chuqing, leading three thousand loose-haired warriors in black armor and corresponding to the Five Stellar Lords of the Northern Pole. Countless soldiers massed beneath the black banners. It was as though frozen clouds cut off the eastern sun, while black vapors swallowed the winds of the Northern Sea.

Seeing this, Zhu Wu said from horseback, “This is the sign of the celestial sphere turning to the left. Today belongs to metal, and the celestial sphere is moving leftward. Troops are certain to come against us.” Before he had finished speaking, five cannon shots thundered at once, and troops came surging out of the opposing formation. p.src: In the central command, Song Jiang brooded over the matter and consulted Lu Junyi and the others: “We lost today’s battle. What are we to do? If we refuse battle again, they will surely come and attack us.” Lu Junyi said, “Tomorrow, have two columns engage the troops covering the rear of their formation; then dispatch two more columns to strike at the seven gates due north; and order the infantry to break in through the center. Then we shall see how strong or weak the interior really is.” Song Jiang said, “That will do.” The next day they acted upon Lu Junyi’s advice, struck camp, advanced to the battlefront, and made ready. The camp gates were thrown wide and the troops marched forth. The Liao army could be seen not far away, and its six rear-guard divisions came scouting toward them from afar. Song Jiang ordered Guan Sheng to the left and Huyan Zhuo to the right, each leading his own command to drive back the Liao rear guard. p.src: Song Jiang again consulted Wu Yong and the others: “Today we have lost Li Kui as well as the battle. If this continues, what can we possibly do?” Wu Yong said, “The young general we captured alive the other day is Commander Wuyan’s son. He is just the man to exchange for Li Kui.” Song Jiang said, “If we exchange him now, how shall we rescue anyone who may be lost later?” Wu Yong replied, “Why are you so stubbornly deluded, brother? For now, attend to the danger before our eyes.” Before he had finished speaking, a junior officer came to report that a Liao general had sent an envoy to parley. Song Jiang summoned him into central command. The foreign officer exchanged courtesies with Song Jiang and said, “I come under our marshal’s orders. Today we captured one of your commanders. When he was brought before our commander-in-chief, he would not have him killed, but gave him ample wine and meat and is treating him well there. The commander wishes to return him to you in exchange for the restoration of his son, the young general; if you consent, General, he will have your commander sent back at once.” Song Jiang said, “If that is so, tomorrow I shall bring the young general before the lines and exchange the two.” The foreign officer received Song Jiang’s answer, mounted his horse, and departed. Song Jiang again consulted Wu Yong: “We have no means of breaking their formation. We had better bring the young general here, use this exchange to make peace, and have both sides cease fighting.” Wu Yong said, “Let the troops rest for the time being. We can devise another sound plan and return to break the enemy; it will not be too late.” At dawn, men were sent with all speed to fetch Wuyan’s young general, while another man went directly to Commander Wuyan to explain the proposal. Now Commander Wuyan was seated in his tent when a soldier came to report that Vanguard Song had sent a man to parley. The commander ordered the man admitted. Brought before the tent, he met Commander Wuyan and said, “Our Vanguard Song presents his respects to Your Excellency. We will now return the young general in exchange for our commander. Since the weather has turned bitterly cold and the soldiers are suffering, let both sides suspend hostilities for the present and discuss matters again next spring, so that men and horses alike may be spared frostbite. We await Your Excellency’s command.” On hearing this, Commander Wuyan roared, “That witless, disgraceful son allowed himself to be captured alive by you! Even if he survives, how could he have the face to see me? There will be no exchange. Take him away and behead him for me! If you want a respite and an end to the fighting, tell your Song Jiang to come and surrender with his hands bound, and I shall spare his life. If he refuses, once I bring my great army down upon you, not a blade of grass will remain!” Then he roared, “Begone!” The envoy galloped back to camp and reported these words to Song Jiang. Alarmed that Li Kui might not be saved, Song Jiang immediately struck camp and set out. Taking Wuyan’s young general with him, he went straight to the front and shouted across the opposing lines, “Release our commander and I will return your young general. It does not matter if there is no truce; we will face you in formation and fight it out.” Presently, from within the Liao ranks, Li Kui was brought out on horseback before the battle line. On this side they likewise led up a horse and sent Wuyan’s young general out beyond the lines. Thus the two sides settled the matter upon a single word. Both sides released and recovered their men at the same moment: General Li returned to camp, while the young general rode across to the other side. Neither side fought again that day. Song Jiang withdrew his troops to camp and for the moment congratulated Li Kui on his safe return.

What are we to do?” Huyan Zhuo said, “Tomorrow we should divide our forces into ten divisions. Let two engage the troops covering the rear of their formation, while the other eight strike together and settle everything in one battle.” Song Jiang said, “Everything depends upon you brothers uniting your hearts and strength. We shall certainly carry out the plan tomorrow.” Wu Yong said, “Twice we have charged without shaking them. We had better hold our ground and wait for them to come and fight.” Song Jiang said, “Waiting for them is no sound plan either. Our brothers must simply oppose them with all their strength. Song Jiang’s troops were caught unprepared. Song Jiang ordered the officers and men to guard the mountain-pass stockade closely, dig the moats deep, plant the chevaux-de-frise firmly, and keep the gates tightly shut without venturing forth, while they endured the winter cold.

p.src: Now Deputy Privy Councillor and Pacification Commissioner Zhao had repeatedly sent memorials to the capital, requesting the dispatch of padded coats and other supplies. The court therefore specially appointed Wang Wenbin—an imperial instructor in spear and staff to the eight hundred thousand Imperial Guards and the incumbent military commissioner of Zhengzhou, a man accomplished in both letters and arms and respected throughout the court—to lead more than ten thousand men from the capital. He requisitioned civilian laborers and carts to convey five hundred thousand padded coats to Vanguard Commander Song's army, where he was to deliver them, urge the officers and troops to press forward in battle, and secure an early victory. Wang Wenbin received the imperial edict and documents, assembled the weapons for his escort, secured the armor, saddles, and horses, hurried the laborers and troops along, and set the wagons in motion. Leaving the Eastern Capital, he advanced toward Chenqiao Station. He supervised one or two hundred carts, each bearing a yellow banner inscribed “Padded Coats Bestowed by the Emperor,” as they wound slowly onward. At every place they passed, the local authorities supplied their provisions. After many days upon the road, he reached the frontier, paid his respects to Privy Councillor Zhao, and presented the official document from the Secretariat. Commissioner Zhao read it and said with great delight, “General, you have come at precisely the right time. At present Vanguard Commander Song has suffered several successive defeats at the hands of Wuyan, commander of the Liao forces, who has arrayed his troops in the ‘All-Encompassing Heaven Formation.’ Many of his leaders have been wounded; they have now been sent here to recuperate under An Daoquan's treatment. Vanguard Commander Song is encamped in the district of Yongqing County and dares not give battle. He is deeply troubled.” Wang Wenbin replied, “It is precisely for this reason that the court sent me to urge the troops forward and secure an early victory. Since our forces have now suffered repeated defeats, if I return to the capital, I shall be hard pressed to report to the officials of the ministries and courts. Though I am a man of little talent, I have read military treatises since childhood and know something of formations. I would go to the front, employ some modest stratagem, and fight one decisive battle, thereby sharing Vanguard Commander Song's burden. I do not know what command Your Excellency may give.” Privy Councillor Zhao was overjoyed and held a wine feast in his honor. He also rewarded the laborers who had escorted the wagons, then ordered Wang Wenbin to forward the padded coats to Song Jiang's army for distribution. Commissioner Zhao first sent a man ahead to inform Vanguard Commander Song.

A poem bears witness:

p.src: Zhao Kuo could but read the books his father wrote; how foolish that Wenbin too should lose his life. In peaceful times, a thousand men boast boldly; when battle comes, not one of them succeeds.

p.src: Meanwhile, Song Jiang remained in camp, brooding and turning over every possibility, yet could devise no way to defeat the Liao army. He abandoned both sleep and food and found no peace even in his dreams. That night, in the depths of winter, the weather was bitterly cold. He became aware that a violent wind had suddenly arisen in the camp and that a chilling air was piercing him. Song Jiang rose and saw a young maid in blue approach and bow with joined hands. Song Jiang asked, “From where have you come, child?” The child replied, “I bear Her Ladyship's sacred command to invite you, General. I must trouble you to come with me at once.” Song Jiang said, “Where is Her Ladyship now?” The child pointed and said, “Not far from here.” Song Jiang followed the child out of the tent. He saw heaven and earth suffused with a single radiance, gold and jade splendor mingling everywhere; a fragrant breeze blew softly and auspicious vapors drifted about, as though it were the weather of the second or third month of spring. After walking scarcely two or three li, he saw a great grove where green pines flourished, emerald cypresses stood in solemn ranks, purple cassias rose tall and graceful, and stone balustrades showed faintly among them. On either side were dense groves and tall bamboo, drooping willows and luxuriant peach trees. Winding along the balustrade and crossing a stone bridge, they came to a vermilion latticework ceremonial gate. Looking up on every side, he saw inner walls washed white, painted rafters and carved beams, vermilion doors studded with gold, and layered eaves of green tile. Shrimp-whisker blinds were rolled up all around, while the front windows bore tortoiseshell latticework. The young maid led Song Jiang in beneath the left-hand gallery and brought him before an east-facing pavilion. She pushed open its vermilion door and asked him to sit inside for a while. When he raised his eyes, cloud-patterned windows stood silent on every side, rosy light filled the steps, celestial blossoms fluttered in profusion, and an unearthly fragrance curled through the air.

p.src: The Mysterious Lady said to Song Jiang, “Several years have passed before I knew it since I bestowed the heavenly books upon you! You have steadfastly upheld loyalty and righteousness and have never once grown lax. Now the Song emperor has ordered you to defeat Liao. How fares the contest?” Song Jiang prostrated himself and reported, “Since Your Ladyship graciously bestowed the heavenly books upon me, I have never treated them lightly or divulged them to anyone. Now, under imperial command to defeat Liao, I unexpectedly encountered Commander Wuyan’s ‘All-Encompassing Celestial Phenomena’ formation and have suffered several defeats. I have no stratagem left to employ and now stand at a moment of dire peril.” The Mysterious Lady said, “Do you understand the method of the ‘All-Encompassing Celestial Phenomena’ formation?” Song Jiang bowed twice more and replied, “I am but an ignorant mortal of the lower world and do not understand its method. I beg Your Ladyship to instruct me.” The Mysterious Lady said, “The principle of this formation lies in gathering the emblems of the positive force. If you merely attack it as you have done, you will never break it. To break it, you must apply the principles by which the elements engender and overcome one another. For example, among the troops under black banners at the front is stationed the Water Star, corresponding to the ‘Five Northern Stars’ in the upper realm. From your Song army choose seven great commanders, with yellow banners, yellow armor, yellow robes, and yellow horses, to smash through the seven gates of the Liao troops’ black-banner formation. Then order one fierce commander, clad in a yellow robe, to charge straight at the Water Star. This embodies earth overcoming water. Next choose eight commanders with white-robed troops to pierce the green-banner formation on their left. This embodies metal overcoming wood. Then choose eight commanders with red-robed troops to pierce the white-banner formation on their right. This embodies fire overcoming metal. Then choose eight commanders with black-banner troops to pierce the red-banner formation in their rear. This embodies water overcoming fire. Then order a body of green-banner troops, led by nine chosen commanders, to charge directly at the chief commander of the central yellow-banner formation. This embodies wood overcoming earth. Choose two more bodies of troops. Have one, bearing embroidered banners and wearing patterned robes, assume the role of ‘Luohou’ and alone break the Liao army’s ‘Sun’ formation. Have the other, bearing plain banners and wearing silver armor, assume the role of ‘Ketu’ and charge straight through the Liao army’s ‘Moon’ formation. Also construct twenty-four thunder carts corresponding to the twenty-four solar terms, mount fire-stones and cannon upon them, and push them straight into the Liao center. Have Gongsun Sheng invoke the orthodox Heavenly Dipper rites of wind and thunder, and charge directly before the Liao ruler’s carriage. Carry out this plan, and it will suffice to win a complete victory. You must not deploy by day; advance only under cover of darkness. You yourself must lead the army, command the center, and urge the troops forward, so that one roll of the drums brings success. You must receive my words in secrecy. Protect the realm and bring peace to the people; harbor neither retreat nor regret. There are limits between heaven and the mortal world; from this day we part forever. One day, amid jeweled towers and golden palaces, we shall meet again elsewhere. You should return swiftly and must not linger here.” She specially ordered the blue-robed attendant to offer tea. When Song Jiang had finished drinking, she told the attendant to escort the Star Lord back to camp at once.
